commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 41 composition defined its five entry-incidence flags as equality against exemplar HTS lines from chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85, conditions with no basis in chapter 41's cited provisions, so the §301/§232/§201/§338 and reciprocal-exclusion branches reading them could never fire for a chapter-41 entry.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 36; diff read, two hunks only. Kind reasoning identical to index 36.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a pure architectural decoupling and could not: the ch37 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are literal equalities against 10-digit statistical reporting numbers in chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95 (e.g. `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"`), conditions that can never be true for an entry routed to a chapter-37 composition, and the surviving consumers then read them as caller inputs. Those flags carry substantive branches in this module (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: entry_is_line_a`, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: entry_is_line_b`, the five-slot `china_301_component_rate` sum, the §201 CSPV and §338/beer slots), whose own proof atoms cite list-membership provisions ("Heading 9903.88.03 applies to all products of China that are classified in the following 8-digit subheadings"), so grounding incidence on one out-of-chapter exemplar line is a formula grounded on the wrong provision, not a missing clause or a scope/entity slip. It is not mechanical: formulas, proof atoms and the input surface all change (the PR comment notes "c and e are fully replaced and no longer valid input slots"), and the next commit in the same PR, a9562cfd4, re-grounds those same references on membership-semantic inputs (`entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, `entry_is_section_201_cspv`, §301 list slots) — removal plus re-grounding, exactly the untraceable_branch pattern. The first reader's kind and reading survive; I would keep confidence just under 0.8 only because this commit performs the removal half and the re-grounding half lands one commit later.

(2) The removed atoms were traceable strings but to the wrong provisions: each cited a real corpus excerpt describing the exemplar line itself ("Footballs", "Beer made from malt", "Crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells"), never a provision this chapter module's action components rest on. That is why untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision") fits better than unrepresented_clause or wrong_entity_or_scope.

(3) Stale text a reviewer may trip on: the post summary still carries the generator boilerplate "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values." That clause describes only the sibling-distinctness serialization step and is contradicted by this diff (atoms removed, five identifiers become caller inputs). Do not read it as evidence of a semantics-preserving change.

(4) Dedup: this commit applies the identical removal to 100 generated chapter modules (module_files[0..99]); ch37 is one instance, and the chapter-72 pilot is called out in the new summary as sharing the input surface. The hand-built witness composition is deliberately untouched and remains the five-line oracle, so the defect is specific to the generated chapters.
